about: Curated outreach knowledge base. Every 'facts' entry paraphrases or briefly quotes the linked page, as fetched on the accessed date. 'related_indicators' and 'channels' are a PROJECT MAPPING (our inference about which dataset indicators an organization's stated work relates to), not claims made by the organization. Sites that could not be reached on 2026-09-27 (e.g. pmjay.gov.in, careindia.org, educategirls.ngo, aajeevika.gov.in) are not used as sources.

organizations.name: Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS, 'JEEViKA')

facts.text: Describes itself as "An Initiative of Government of Bihar for Poverty Alleviation" and as the State Rural Livelihoods Mission, Bihar.
Its website is branded under the Rural Development Department, Government of Bihar, and references a women's employment scheme ('Mahila Rojgar Yojana') and NRLM e-governance.

organizations.unverified_note: The pages fetched did not state the number of self-help groups, households or districts covered.

organizations.name: Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHA), National Health Mission

facts.text: A component of the National Rural Health Mission is to provide every village with a trained female community health activist (ASHA), selected from the village itself.

ASHAs act as an interface between the community and the public health system: creating health awareness, first-contact care and referrals, counselling women on birth preparedness and safe delivery, and working with ANMs and Anganwadi workers.

organizations.name: Mission Saksham Anganwadi & POSHAN 2.0, Ministry of Women and Child Development

facts.text: The Ministry of Women and Child Development's website lists 'Mission Saksham Anganwadi & POSHAN 2.0' as a key scheme and identifies 'Pregnant/lactating women and children (0-6 years)' as a user group.

organizations.name: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)

facts.text: A national public health insurance scheme of the Government of India, administered by the National Health Authority, giving a cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for treatment in empanelled public and private hospitals.
Targets roughly the economically bottom 50% of the population; later expanded to all citizens aged 70 and above.

organizations.source_type: secondary source (Wikipedia); the official site pmjay.gov.in could not be reached

facts.text: Run by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, as 'a National Mission on Financial Inclusion' aiming for at least one basic bank account for every household.
Provides a basic savings bank account, access to need-based credit, remittances, insurance and pension, a RuPay debit card, and channels government benefits through Direct Benefit Transfer.

geography.detail: States '110+ districts in India'; regional offices in New Delhi, Ranchi and Chennai. The homepage does not name Bihar.

facts.text: Builds participatory, voice-based media platforms (IVR and community radio) so that communities can share information and opinions.
Says it serves hard-to-reach and rural communities, including women, agricultural workers, industrial workers and youth, in '110+ Districts in India'.

geography.detail: States that it works in '24 states & union territories'; the homepage does not list them.

facts.text: Describes itself as one of the largest NGOs in India (since 1995), focused on education.
Runs the 'Pratham-Jameel Second Chance Program' for girls and women returning to education, and reports reaching 208 thousand girls and women through mothers' groups and second-chance initiatives.

geography.detail: States work with 3.4 million households in 145 districts and 9 states; the homepage names locations in Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh. Bihar is not mentioned on the page.

facts.text: Works with 'the most marginalized people, especially rural women', mobilizing women into self-help groups and linking them to banks, markets and government services.
States that it works with 3.4 million households across 145 districts in 9 states of India.

organizations.name: Prasar Bharati (Doordarshan and All India Radio / Akashvani)

geography.detail: Includes regional Doordarshan channels across states and languages.

facts.text: India's public service broadcaster, an autonomous body under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, comprising Doordarshan (television, including regional channels) and All India Radio / Akashvani.
Distributes content through traditional broadcast, satellite (DD Free Dish) and digital platforms.
